result.summary: WF-01 micro-amendment after the code design of M1.3, by decisions/0118 О2 and О17 and the wording points N7, N9, N10 of decisions/0116 О25, and only by them (N11 needs no edit). REQ-108 criterion 14: the one console line Chrome writes for a page answered with 404 or 503 is now declared exactly — level error, the text with that status, the page's own path — and must come exactly once in each load of /nope and of the gate page; any other line, the same line twice, an exception, a rejected promise, a CSP violation, or a declared line that does not come fails; / of the open site writes no line at all. REQ-108 criterion 2 (and REQ-109 criterion 10, which repeats it): an empty test step no longer passes — each test step must print «# tests N» with N above 0 and equal to the count of its folder in the run's test catalogue (counted as the runner counts), and two presence guards cross the steps (npmrc.test.js reads the 10 int and 2 pg files, node-main.test.js the 14 unit files, all named by the criteria); RELEASE-VALIDATOR plants four more cases. N7: criterion 13 and the description no longer say «never a missed password»; the measured misses of the search are named (a literal password starting with `${`, and two more forms measured here: an empty user and the upper-case scheme); the command is unchanged. N9: REQ-109 now states, from Vercel's documentation read by the gate and again by me, that a redeploy of a deployment built from source rebuilds it and picks up a changed variable (only a --prebuilt one is reused); spike S1 still measures it. N10: the Q12 lines and the REQ-108 design pointers name decisions/0116 О1-О26 and decisions/0118. Every changed rule was tried on a copy of the design's sketch outside the project: 7 trials of the guards and the count (the empty folder and both-empty cases pass the old counts and fail only the new count rule), 30 real browser loads green and 9 planted twins red for criterion 14, 13 planted lines for the secret search. Only the blocks REQ-108 and REQ-109 changed (the rest of the file byte for byte, two hash methods); format, handoffs-check and traces are clean.
